App details

Inventory / ReadyStock

Keep track of supplies at home, in a workshop or in a small business, offline.

In the worksPlannedAndroid

What it’s for

Keep track of food, household supplies and workshop parts, including their quantities, storage places and expiry dates. Use low-stock views and restock lists, and estimate reserve duration from your own consumption rates. Barcode and text recognition on the device help with entry; you confirm suggested details.

Main features

  • Quantities, storage locations and expiry dates.
  • Low-stock alerts and automatic restock lists.
  • Barcode and on-device text recognition help with entry.
  • Estimate how long reserves will last from your rates.

This app is being planned and is not yet available to download. The description presents its intended functions.

Features in detail

Organise stock, expiry and replenishment

Several inventories, items and units

Create separate home, pantry, workshop or emergency inventories. Give each item a name, stock unit and optional note, category, minimum and target. Units include pieces, kg/g, L/mL, metres, packs/boxes and your own units. Define package relationships yourself, such as one carton equals 12 pieces; unrelated units are not silently converted.

Batches, stock changes and history

Keep different expiry dates and storage locations as separate batches of one item. Add, consume, transfer, correct or discard expired stock; totals update from these changes. Quick actions offer undo through a recorded correction. Name categories and locations, reuse your own item templates and archive items; deletion with history needs confirmation.

Minimum, target and replenishment list

Set minimum and optional target stock. Zero or low stock is highlighted and below-minimum items enter the refill list; needed quantity reaches the target, or minimum when no target exists. Add manual shopping entries, check purchases and turn a bought item into stock-in; the list recalculates after each change.

Expiry warnings and using older stock first

Enter optional batch expiry and choose days/weeks/months of warning or turn reminders off. Consumption suggests the earliest expiring batch first; without dates it suggests the oldest acquired stock. Dated batches come before undated ones; equal expiry uses acquisition order. You can override the suggestion, and it changes no stock until confirmed.

Consumption, coverage days and emergency targets

Enter your quantity used per chosen period to estimate days of stock. View total coverage or usable coverage excluding expired batches; without a positive rate, days are unavailable. Optional emergency targets use your chosen days, and household size only when the rate is explicitly per person. Rates and expiry are not required for ordinary inventories.

Local barcode and text recognition

Scan EAN-8, EAN-13, UPC-A or UPC-E to find an item you previously linked, or enter data for an unknown code. Recognise a label, packaging or receipt from camera/chosen image for proposed name, quantity and expiry. Edit or reject each field and confirm before stock changes. Scanning can start stock-in or consumption; manual entry always remains available, with no online product database required.

Dashboard, searching and reminders

Tap dashboard counts to open active, zero/low, expired/expiring or replenishment lists. Search and filter by inventory, category, location and archive status; sort by name, stock, expiry, location or status. Optional alerts can be turned off globally or per expiry item. Denying Android notifications does not prevent managing stock.

Spreadsheet import, export and full backup

Import the documented emergency-stock XLSX columns or supported CSV, preview name, rate, quantity, expiry, place and notes, then confirm validated changes. Export JSON, CSV or XLSX for your chosen destination. Full offline backup/restore preserves related records and previews compatibility before replacement; a spreadsheet export alone is not necessarily a complete backup.

Local data and your confirmed choices

Inventory and recognition work locally without an account or server-side image analysis. Camera access is requested for scanning, not manual stock entry. Corrected barcode/text associations can be reused as editable local suggestions; source pictures are not automatically kept as long-term stock records. A failed save is shown as a failure, not a successful stock change.

Just in case

Tap the About logo seven times: supplies fill a shelf one by one until it becomes crowded and bends slightly. This offline joke changes no real inventory, quantities or reminders.

Use, settings and availability

Offline use

The main functions are designed to work on your device without a JN86 account. Ads, purchases and external links may need internet.

Language, settings and help

Choose one of eight app languages and adjust the available settings. About provides privacy information and a link to voluntary JN86 support. Support does not unlock paid functions. Availability is shown below.

Ads and optional ad removal

All described functions are planned to be free, with banner ads and optional one-time Google Play ad removal. No subscription is planned. The purchase screen shows the actual local price; purchase restoration uses Google Play.

Availability

This app is being created. The features described here are planned; it is not yet available to download.
